evidence.quote: Penalizes large errors heavily (quadratic). Sensitive to outliers. The default loss for regression.
Smooth combination of MSE (small errors) and MAE (large errors). Robust to outliers while remaining differentiable. Often used in regression losses for deep learning.
A common pattern: train with **Huber loss** (smooth like MSE near zero, robust like MAE for large errors), evaluate with MAE or RMSE.
evidence.source_path: 03 - Machine Learning/03.6 - Model Evaluation/03. Regression Metrics - MAE, MSE, RMSE, R2, MAPE.md

evidence.quote: MSE and MAE are both loss functions (used in training) and metrics (used in evaluation).
evidence.source_path: 03 - Machine Learning/03.6 - Model Evaluation/03. Regression Metrics - MAE, MSE, RMSE, R2, MAPE.md

evidence.quote: you might train with MSE (for smooth gradients) but evaluate with MAE (for interpretability and robustness). This is fine — the loss determines what the model optimizes; the metric determines how you judge it.
evidence.source_path: 03 - Machine Learning/03.6 - Model Evaluation/03. Regression Metrics - MAE, MSE, RMSE, R2, MAPE.md

evidence.quote: - The gradient is constant magnitude regardless of error size, which can make training harder (the model gets the same "push" from a small error as a large one). This is why MAE is rarely used as a training loss, even when it is the evaluation metric.
